Alumette is a VR short animation film, in the same vein as The Rose and I, except it's loosely based on a tale by Andersen instead of The Little Prince.

The story is nothing to write home about, and the whole experience isn't interactive at all, but the exquisite animation and immersion provided by VR still makes it an essential addition to one's VR library. It's also a good title to introduce your friend and family to VR for the first time, because it is quiet (no risk of motion sickness) and requires no control to master.

A VR short movie which is well done and definitely worth checking out for the feels. Can't say I would pay for it though, since the story end abruptly and is incomplete. That, and there isn't any interactivity to the experience (well, other than head tracking to get different perspectives).
Such a beautiful story. Sad but beautiful.

A lovely 15-minute film.  I didn't find it as emotional as most reviewers because I know "The Little Match Girl" that this is clearly based off of; kindof spoiled the ending.  It does stoke my excitement for the future of VR films, though!  This is a good start.
Sad story but very well done, shows the power of VR for animated movies :) Yes, I'm looking at you, Disney!
